f69216980d.s:
ಮಾಸಸಂಜ್ಞೇಯದಾ ಋಕ್ಷೇ ಚನ್ದ್ರಃ ಸಮ್ಪೂರ್ಣಮಣ್ಡಲಃ।  
ಗುರುಣಾ ಯದಿ ಸಂಯುಕ್ತಃ ಸಾ ತಿಥಿರ್ಮಹತೀ ಸ್ಮೃತಾ॥  
ಪೌರ್ಣಮಾಸ್ಯಾಂ ಚನ್ದ್ರಃ ತನ್ಮಾಸನಕ್ಷತ್ರೇ ಚಿತ್ರಾದೌ ಗುರುಣಾ ಯುಕ್ತಶ್ಚೇತ್ ಸಾ ಪೌರ್ಣಮಾಸೀ ಮಹಾಚೈತ್ರ್ಯಾದಿಸಂಜ್ಞೇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ।    
  
ಮಹಾಚೈತ್ರ್ಯಾದಿಷು ಕೃತಂ ದಾನಂ ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಮುಪೋಷಣಮ್।  
ಅನನ್ತಫಲದಂ ಪ್ರಾಹುರ್ಮುನಯೋ ಧರ್ಮವೇದಿನಃ॥  
---ಸ್ಮೃತಿಮುಕ್ತಾಫಲೇ ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಕಾಣ್ಡೇ ಉತ್ತರಭಾಗೇ

f6a02bb3dc.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between śaniḥ and śukraḥ in uttaraprōṣṭhapadā mīnaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°54′41.54″.
f6a02bb3dc.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°54′41.54″, 0°54′28.77″ apart, disc-to-disc. śaniḥ at uttaraprōṣṭhapadā-2 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°07′32.90″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.97, elongation 14°48′02.24″ E). śukraḥ at uttaraprōṣṭhapadā-2 mīnaḥ (latitude 1°12′51.36″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.90, elongation 14°41′58.92″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śaniḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over śukraḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.
f6a02bb3dc.s:

f7088ceeba.d:
Shortly after bAjI rAv 2's surrender to the British, and the British victory over shiNDe forces; yashvantrAv holkar separately (re)started his fight but settled for a treaty with the British.

He was initially successful, but was chased and defeated by General Lake - more by diplomacy than battle. The jAT rAjA raNajIt singh briefly helped, but defected when pressed. daulatrAv shiNDe joined briefly but was soon bought off. Other such as raNajIt singh of panjAb, hill chiefs, even the afhAn shAh etc.. all backed off and stayed away. 

He would write two years later to vyankojI bhosle: " I paid a visit to Daulatrao and explained to him how important it was for all of us to join to avert foreign domination. Daulatrao failed me. It was cooperation and good will which had built the Maratha state. But now, we have all become self seekers. You also did not make your promise good. It is no use now talking of past things. When I found myself abandoned on all sides, I accepted the offer the British agents brought to me and concluded the war."

f7254026a2.d:
The Shukla-paksha Ekadashi of śrāvaṇa month is known as śravaṇa-putradā-ēkādaśī.

The fruits of fasting on Ekādaśī are greatly extolled in the Padma Purana—

A person who bathes at Śaṃkhoddhāra and beholds the image of Viṣṇu does not acquire even a sixteenth of the merit earned by fasting on Ekādaśī. O noble king, even if one gives four lakhs of coins on the days of the Sun's transition between Zodiac signs, it does not equal even a sixteenth of the merit from an Ekādaśī fast! Indeed, fasting on Ekādaśī grants the same religious merit as bathing at Prabhāsa during a lunar or solar eclipse. One who drinks the sacred water at Kedāra is freed from rebirth, and likewise, fasting on Ekādaśī removes the cycle of rebirth.

The merit from an Ekādaśī fast is a hundred times greater than the reward of performing an Ashvamedha sacrifice on earth. Fasting on Ekādaśī yields a hundredfold more merit than gifting a thousand cows to a learned brāhmaṇa. Those who fast on Ekādaśī are considered equal to those whose bodies are inhabited by Brahma, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. The merit from observing the Ekādaśī vow is immeasurable, and difficult to obtain even by the Devas. There is no other vow like that of the Ekādaśī, that destroys sins.
f7254026a2.s:
ಪಕ್ಷೇ ಪಕ್ಷೇ ಚ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಮುಪೋಷಣಮ್।  
ಯದೀಚ್ಛೇದ್ವಿಷ್ಣುಸಾಯುಜ್ಯಂ ಶ್ರಿಯಂ ಸನ್ತತಿಮಾತ್ಮನಃ।  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಂ ನ ಭುಞ್ಜೀತ ಪಕ್ಷಯೋರುಭಯೋರಪಿ॥  
  
ಅದ್ಯ ಸ್ಥಿತ್ವಾ ನಿರಾಹಾರಃ ಶ್ವೋಭೂತೇ ಪರಮೇಶ್ವರ।  
ಭೋಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಿ ಪುಣ್ಡರೀಕಾಕ್ಷ ಶರಣಂ ಮೇ ಭವಾಚ್ಯುತ॥  
ಪ್ರಮಾದಾದಥವಾಽಽಲಸ್ಯಾದ್ಧರೇ ಕೇಶವ ಮಾಧವ।  
ವ್ರತಸ್ಯಾಸ್ಯ ಚ ವೈ ವಿಘ್ನೋ ನ ಭವೇತ್ತ್ವತ್ಪ್ರಸಾದತಃ॥  
--ಪದ್ಮಪುರಾಣೇ  
  
ಶ್ರೀಬ್ರಹ್ಮವೈವರ್ತೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಖಣ್ಡೇ ಸೌತಿಶೌನಕಸಂವಾದೇ ನಾರದಂ ಪ್ರತಿ ಶಿವೋಪದೇಶೇ ಭಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಭಕ್ಷ್ಯಾದಿವಿವರಣಂ ನಾಮ ಸಪ್ತವಿಂಶತಿತಮೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯಃ---  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯಾಮನಾಹಾರಂ ಗೃಹೀ ವಿಪ್ರಶ್ಚ ಭಾರತೇ।  
ಸ ಚ ತಿಷ್ಠತಿ ವೈಕುಣ್ಠೇ ಯಾವದ್ವೈ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣೋ ವಯಃ॥೧೪॥  
  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಫಲಂ ಪ್ರೋಕ್ತಂ ಪಾದ್ಮಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಶಙ್ಖೋದ್ಧಾರೇ ನರಃ ಸ್ನಾತ್ವಾ ದೃಷ್ಟ್ವಾ ದೇವಂ ಗದಾಧರಮ್॥೩೫॥  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಸ್ಯ ಕಲಾಂ ನಾರ್ಹತಿ ಷೋಡಶೀಮ್।  
ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತಿಷು ಚತುರ್ಲಕ್ಷಂ ಯೋ ದದಾತಿ ನೃಪೋತ್ತಮ॥೩೬॥  
ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಸ್ಯ ಕಲಾಂ ನಾರ್ಹತಿ ಷೋಡಶೀಮ್।  
ಪ್ರಭಾಸಕ್ಷೇತ್ರೇ ಯತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ಗ್ರಹಣೇ ಚನ್ದ್ರಸೂರ್ಯಯೋಃ॥೩೭॥  
ತತ್ಫಲಂ ಜಾಯತೇ ನೂನಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಕೇದಾರೇ ಚೋದಕಂ ಪೀತ್ವಾ ಪುನರ್ಜನ್ಮ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ॥೩೮॥  
ತಥಾ ಚೈಕಾದಶೀ ಪಾರ್ಥ ಗರ್ಭವಾಸಕ್ಷಯಙ್ಕರೀ।  
ಅಶ್ವಮೇಧಸ್ಯ ಯಜ್ಞಸ್ಯ ಪೃಥಿವ್ಯಾಂ ಯತ್ಫಲಂ ಲಭೇತ್॥೩೯॥  
ತಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛತಗುಣಂ ಪುಣ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ತಪಸ್ವಿನೋ ಗೃಹೇ ಯಸ್ಯ ಭುಞ್ಜತೇ ಚ ದ್ವಿಜೋತ್ತಮಾಃ॥೪೦॥  
ತತ್ಫಲಂ ಜಾಯತೇ ನೂನಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಗೋಸಹಸ್ರೇಣ ಯತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ದತ್ವಾ ವೇದಾನ್ತಪಾರಗೇ॥೪೧॥  
ತಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛತಗುಣಂ ಪುಣ್ಯಮೇಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ಯೇಷಾಂ ದೇಹೇ ತ್ರಯೋ ದೇವಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವಿಷ್ಣುಮಹೇಶ್ವರಾಃ॥೪೨॥  
ವಸನ್ತಿ ತೇಷಾಂ ತೇ ತುಲ್ಯಾ ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುಪವಾಸಿನಃ।  
ತೇ ನರಾಃ ಪುಣ್ಯಕರ್ಮಾಣೋ ಯೇ ಭಕ್ತಾ ಹರಿಪೂಜಕಾಃ॥೪೩॥  
ಏಕಾದಶೀವ್ರತಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಪುಣ್ಯಸಙ್ಖ್ಯಾ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ।  
ಏತತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ಭವೇತ್ ತಸ್ಯ ಯತ್ಸುರೈರಪಿ ದುರ್ಲಭಮ್॥೪೪॥  
ಏಕಾದಶೀಸಮಂ ನಾಸ್ತಿ ವ್ರತಂ ಪಾಪಪ್ರಣಾಶನಮ್॥೧೧೮॥  
---ಶ್ರೀಪಾದ್ಮೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ ಪಞ್ಚಪಞ್ಚಾಶತ್ಸಾಹಸ್ರ್ಯಾಂ ಸಂಹಿತಾಯಾಮುತ್ತರಖಣ್ಡೇ ಉಮಾಮಹೇಶ್ವರಸಂವಾದೇ ಏಕಾದಶ್ಯುತ್ಪತ್ತಿ-ಮುರವಧೋ ನಾಮ ಚತ್ವಾರಿಂಶೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯಃ॥೪೦॥

f7430dd19f.d:
Mulraj Chopra, the khatri divAn at multAn loyal to raNajIt singh and family, rebelled against the British on this day.

The revolt was started by a soldier from mUlarAja's family attacking and wounding two British officers who'd come to take over.

The poet Hakim Chand recites: Then the mother of Mulraj spoke to him reminding him of the Sikh Gurus and martyrs: 'I will kill myself leaving a curse on your head. Either lead your men to death or get out of my sight; (and) I shall undertake the Khalsa army and go to the battle ...'. She tied a bracelet on his wrist and sent him to the battle. Next morning, the mob hacked the two British officers to death. Mulraj presented Vans Agnew's head to Vitesh Sharma and told him to take it back to Currie at Lahore.

Aftermath: 
The British chief Currie sent a big detachment of the khalsa under Sher Singh Attariwalla to help the Bengal army in beseiging Multan. However, Sher Singh rebelled as well on Sep 14! However, Sher Singh moved away to fight separately. Mulraj was however defeated by 22nd January. This freed up more artillery for the Birish to use during the decisive Battle of Gujarat.

f7c51f843c.s:
ಸ್ಮೃತ್ಯನ್ತರೇ---  
ಅಮಾ ಸೋಮೇನ ಭೌಮೇನ ಗುರುಣಾ ವಾ ಯುತಾ ಯದಿ।  
ಸಾ ತಿಥಿಃ ಪುಷ್ಕಲಾ ನಾಮ ಸೂರ್ಯಗ್ರಹಣಸನ್ನಿಭಾ॥

f7db1a6703.b: Total lunar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈12.0 of 12 aṅgulas), Moon at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
f7db1a6703.d: The eclipse is still in progress at moonset (grastAstamana). Umbral magnitude: 1.15 (parimāṇa ≈12.0 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 15:25►06:44 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra maghā/pūrvaphalgunī/uttaraphalgunī (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or pūrvāṣāḍhā (anujanma) or apabharaṇī (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: siṁhaḥ, kanyā, makaraḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ get more ashubha phala, dhanuḥ, kumbhaḥ, mēṣaḥ, karkaṭaḥ somewhat ashubha, tulā, vr̥śchikaḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam shubha phala. Falling on a Monday, this is an especially auspicious chūḍāmaṇi (crest-jewel) eclipse. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
f7db1a6703.r: - Food-restriction timing and graha-shanti nakshatra/rashi lists follow this pancAnga's "General notes for all grahanas" instructions.

f81a2847ef.d: On this day, Kunwar Singh, masterfully deceiving the british forces, crossed gangA into bihAr. He had spread word that there are no boats and that he would cross the river with elephants at a different spot, even as he gathered boats at a differnt point. Douglas' army caught up and began to shoot at their boat. One of the bullets shattered Singh's left wrist. Singh felt that his hand had become useless and that there was the additional risk of infection due to the bullet-shot. He drew his sword and cut off his left hand near the elbow and offered it to the Ganges.

f81d00325c.d: Amāvāsyā of bhādrapada month. This is extremely special and is known as mahālaya.
f81d00325c.s:
ಸ್ಮೃತ್ಯನ್ತರೇ---  
ಅಮಾ ಪಾತಶ್ಚ ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತಿಸ್ತಥಾ ವೈಧೃತಿರೇವ ಚ।  
ಅಷ್ಟಕಾಶ್ಚೈವ ಮನ್ವಾದಿರ್ಯುಗಾದಿಶ್ಚ ಮಹಾಲಯಃ॥  
ಚನ್ದ್ರಸೂರ್ಯೋಪರಾಗಶ್ಚ ಗಜಚ್ಛಾಯಾ ತಥೈವ ಚ।  
ದ್ರವ್ಯಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಸಮ್ಪತ್ತಿಃ ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಕಾಲಾಃ ಪ್ರಕೀರ್ತಿತಾಃ॥  
ಮಾರ್ಕಣ್ಡೇಯಃ---  
ಕನ್ಯಾಗತೇ ಸವಿತರಿ ದಿನಾನಿ ದಶ ಪಞ್ಚ ಚ।  
ಪಾರ್ವಣೇನೈವ ವಿಧಿನಾ ತತ್ರ ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಂ ವಿಧೀಯತೇ॥  
ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಂ ಕುರ್ವನ್ನಮಾವಾಸ್ಯಾಮನ್ನೇನ ಪುರುಷಃ ಶುಚಿಃ।  
ಸರ್ವಾನ್ ಕಾಮಾನವಾಪ್ನೋತಿ ಸ್ವರ್ಗಂ ವಾಽತ್ಯನ್ತಮಶ್ನುತೇ॥

f82670ae54.b: Partial solar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈6.3 of 12 aṅgulas), Sun at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
f82670ae54.d: Magnitude: 52% of the solar diameter is covered (parimāṇa ≈6.3 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 03:21►17:44 (from 4 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra punarvasuḥ/puṣyaḥ/āśrēṣā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or anūrādhā (anujanma) or uttaraprōṣṭhapadā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: karkaṭaḥ, siṁhaḥ, dhanuḥ, mēṣaḥ get more ashubha phala, vr̥śchikaḥ, makaraḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam somewhat ashubha, kanyā, tulā, kumbhaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
f82670ae54.r: - Food-restriction timing and graha-shanti nakshatra/rashi lists follow this pancAnga's "General notes for all grahanas" instructions.

f83550dc94.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in āśrēṣā karkaṭaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°30′36.04″.
f83550dc94.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°30′36.04″, 0°30′28.72″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at āśrēṣā-3 karkaṭaḥ (latitude 1°44′30.89″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -2.04, elongation 1°45′13.84″ W). śukraḥ at āśrēṣā-3 karkaṭaḥ (latitude 1°13′54.85″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 1°14′55.59″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.
f83550dc94.s:
ಭಾವಾಭಾವಾಯ ಲೋಕಾನಾಂ ಕಲ್ಪನೇಯಂ ಪ್ರದರ್ಶಿತಾ।  
ಸ್ವಮಾರ್ಗಗಾಃ ಪ್ರಯಾನ್ತ್ಯೇತೇ ದೂರಮನ್ಯೋನ್ಯಮಾಶ್ರಿತಾಃ॥  
--ಸೂರ್ಯಸಿದ್ಧಾನ್ತೇ  
  
ಷಣ್ಮಾಸಂ ಗ್ರಹಭಿನ್ನಭಂ ತ್ಯಜ ಶುಭೇ ಯೌದ್ಧಂ ತಥೋತ್ಪಾತಭಮ್।  
--ಮುಹೂರ್ತಚಿನ್ತಾಮಣೌ (ನಾರದಸಂಹಿತಾನುಸಾರೇಣ)

f85422c445.s:
ಯಾಸ್ತಿಸ್ರಸ್ತಿಥಯಃ ಪುಣ್ಯಾ ಅನ್ತಿಕೇ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷಕೇ।  
ಕಾರ್ತಿಕೇ ಮಾಸಿ ವಿಪ್ರೇನ್ದ್ರ ಪೂರ್ಣಿಮಾನ್ತಾಃ ಶುಭಾವಹಾಃ॥೧॥  
ಅನ್ತಿಪುಷ್ಕರಿಣೀ ಸಂಜ್ಞಾ ಸರ್ವಪಾಪಕ್ಷಯಾವಹಾ।  
ಕಾರ್ತಿಕೇ ಮಾಸಿ ಸಮ್ಪೂರ್ಣಂ ಯೋ ವೈ ಸ್ನಾನಂ ಕರೋತಿ ಹ॥೨॥  
ತಿಥಿಷ್ವೇತಾಸು ಸಃ ಸ್ನಾನಾತ್ಪೂರ್ಣಮೇವ ಫಲಂ ಲಭೇತ್।  
ಸರ್ವೇ ವೇದಾಸ್ತ್ರಯೋದಶ್ಯಾಂ ಗತ್ವಾ ಜನ್ತೂನ್ ಪುನನ್ತಿ ಹಿ॥೩॥  
ಚತುರ್ದಶ್ಯಾಂ ಸಯಜ್ಞಾಶ್ಚ ದೇವಾ ಜನ್ತೂನ್ ಪುನನ್ತಿ ಹಿ।  
ಪೂರ್ಣಿಮಾಯಾಂ ಸುತೀರ್ಥಾನಿ ವಿಷ್ಣುನಾ ಸಂಸ್ಥಿತಾನಿ ಹಿ॥೪॥  
ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಘ್ನಾನ್ ವಾ ಸುರಾಪಾನ್ ವಾ ಸರ್ವಾನ್ ಜನ್ತೂನ್ ಪುನನ್ತಿ ಹಿ।  
ಉಷ್ಣೋದಕೇನ ಯಃ ಸ್ನಾಯಾತ್ಕಾರ್ತಿಕ್ಯಾದಿದಿನತ್ರಯೇ॥೫॥  
ರೌರವಂ ನರಕಂ ಯಾತಿ ಯಾವದಿನ್ದ್ರಾಶ್ಚತುರ್ದಶ।  
ಆಮಾಸನಿಯಮಾಶಕ್ತಃ ಕುರ್ಯಾದೇತದ್ದಿನತ್ರಯೇ॥೬॥  
ತೇನ ಪೂರ್ಣಫಲಂ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯ ಮೋದತೇ ವಿಷ್ಣುಮನ್ದಿರೇ।  
ಯೋ ವೈ ದೇವಾನ್ಪಿತೄನ್ವಿಷ್ಣುಂ ಗುರುಮುದ್ದಿಶ್ಯ ಮಾನವಃ॥೭॥  
ನ ಸ್ನಾನಾದಿ ಕರೋತ್ಯದ್ಧಾ ಸ ಯಾತಿ ನರಕಂ ಧ್ರುವಮ್।  
ಕುಟುಮ್ಬಭೋಜನಂ ಯಸ್ತು ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಸ್ತು ದಿನತ್ರಯೇ॥೮॥  
ಸರ್ವಾನ್ಪಿತೄನ್ಸಮುದ್ಧೃತ್ಯ ಸ ಯಾತಿ ಪರಮಂ ಪದಮ್।  
ಗೀತಾಪಾಠಂ ತು ಯಃ ಕುರ್ಯಾದನ್ತಿಮೇ ಚ ದಿನತ್ರಯೇ॥೯॥  
ದಿನೇದಿನೇಽಶ್ವಮೇಧಾನಾಂ ಫಲಮೇತಿ ನ ಸಂಶಯಃ।  
ಸಹಸ್ರನಾಮಪಠನಂ ಯಃ ಕುರ್ಯಾತ್ತು ದಿನತ್ರಯೇ॥೧೦॥  
ನ ಪಾಪೈರ್ಲಿಪ್ಯತೇ ಕ್ವಾಪಿ ಪದ್ಮಪತ್ರಮಿವಾಮ್ಭಸಾ।  
ದೇವತ್ವಂ ಮನುಜೈಃ ಕೈಶ್ಚಿತ್ಕೈಶ್ಚಿತ್ಸಿದ್ಧತ್ವಮೇವ ಚ॥೧೧॥  
ತಸ್ಯ ಪುಣ್ಯಫಲಂ ವಕ್ತುಂ ಕಃ ಶಕ್ತೋ ದಿವಿ ವಾ ಭುವಿ।  
ಯೋ ವೈ ಭಾಗವತಂ ಶಾಸ್ತ್ರಂ ಶೃಣೋತಿ ಚ ದಿನತ್ರಯಮ್॥೧೨॥  
ಕೈಶ್ಚಿತ್ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಭಾವೋ ದಿನತ್ರಯನಿಷೇವಣಾತ್।  
ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಜ್ಞಾನೇನ ವಾ ಮುಕ್ತಿಃ ಪ್ರಯಾಗಮರಣೇನ ವಾ॥೧೩॥  
ಅಥ ವಾ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕೇ ಮಾಸಿ ದಿನತ್ರಯನಿಷೇವಣಾತ್।  
ಕಾರ್ತಿಕೇ ಹರಿಪೂಜಾಂ ತು ಯಃ ಕರೋತಿ ದಿನತ್ರಯೇ॥೧೪॥  
ನ ತಸ್ಯ ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತಿಃ ಕಲ್ಪಕೋಟಿಶತೈರಪಿ।  
ಕಾರ್ತಿಕೇ ಮಾಸಿ ವಿಪ್ರೇನ್ದ್ರ ಸರ್ವಮನ್ತ್ಯದಿನತ್ರಯೇ॥೧೫॥  
ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ತತ್ರಾಪಿ ವೈಶೇಷ್ಯಂ ರಾಕಾಯಾಂ ವರ್ತತೇಽನಘ।  
ಪ್ರಾತಃಕಾಲೇ ಸಮುತ್ಥಾಯ ಶೌಚಂ ಸ್ನಾನಾದಿಕಂ ಚರೇತ್॥೧೬॥  
ಸಮಾಪ್ಯ ಸರ್ವಕರ್ಮಾಣಿ ವಿಷ್ಣುಪೂಜಾಂ ಸಮಾಚರೇತ್।  
ಉದ್ಯಾನೇ ವಾ ಗೃಹೇ ವಾಽಪಿ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕ್ಯಾಂ ವಿಷ್ಣುತತ್ಪರಃ॥೧೭॥  
ಮಣ್ಡಪಂ ತತ್ರ ಕುರ್ವೀತ ಕದಲೀಸ್ತಮ್ಭಮಣ್ಡಿತಮ್।  
ಚೂತಪಲ್ಲವಸಂವೀತಮಿಕ್ಷುದಣ್ಡೈಃ ಸುಮಣ್ಡಿತಮ್॥೧೮॥  
ಚಿತ್ರವಸ್ತ್ರೈಃ ಸ್ವಲಙ್ಕೃತ್ಯ ತತ್ರ ದೇವಂ ಪ್ರಪೂಜಯೇತ್।  
ಚೂತಪಲ್ಲವಪುಷ್ಪಾಢ್ಯೈಃ ಫಲಾದ್ಯೈಃ ಪೂಜಯೇದ್ಧರಿಮ್॥೧೯॥  
ಶೃಣುಯಾದೂರ್ಜಮಾಹಾತ್ಮ್ಯಂ ನಿಯಮೇನ ಶುಚಿಃ ಪುಮಾನ್।  
ಸಮ್ಪೂರ್ಣಮಥ ವಾಽಧ್ಯಾಯಮೇಕಶ್ಲೋಕಮಥಾಪಿ ವಾ॥೨೦॥  
ಮುಹೂರ್ತಂ ವಾಽಪಿ ಶೃಣುಯಾತ್ಕಥಾಂ ಪುಣ್ಯಾಂ ದಿನೇದಿನೇ।  
ಯದಿ ಪ್ರತಿದಿನಂ ಶ್ರೋತುಮಶಕ್ತಃ ಸ್ಯಾತ್ತು ಮಾನವಃ॥೨೧॥  
ಪುಣ್ಯಮಾಸೇಽಥವಾ ಪುಣ್ಯತಿಥೌ ಸಂಶೃಣುಯಾದಪಿ।  
ತೇನ ಪುಣ್ಯಪ್ರಭಾವೇನ ಪಾಪಾನ್ಮುಕ್ತೋ ಭವೇನ್ನರಃ॥೨೨॥  
---ಸ್ಕಾನ್ದ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ ವೈಷ್ಣವಖಣ್ಡೇ ಷಡ್ತ್ರಿಂಶೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯಃ

As stated in the Mahābhārata:

f86845a693.s:
ವೈಶಾಖಮಾಸಸ್ಯ ತು ಯಾ ತೃತೀಯಾಽನವದ್ಯಾಽಸೌ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷೇ ।  
ನಭಸ್ಯಮಾಸಸ್ಯ ಚ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷೇ ತ್ರಯೋದಶೀ ಪಞ್ಚದಶೀ ಚ ಮಾಘೇ॥೧೪-೧೧೦-೨೮॥  
ಉಪಪ್ಲವೇ ಚನ್ದ್ರಮಸೋ ರವೇಶ್ಚ ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಸ್ಯ ಕಾಲೋ ಹ್ಯಯನದ್ವಯೇ ಚ ।  
ಪಾನೀಯಮಪ್ಯತ್ರ ತಿಲೈರ್ವಿಮಿಶ್ರಂ ದದ್ಯಾತ್ಪಿತೃಭ್ಯಃ ಪ್ರಯತೋ ಮನುಷ್ಯಃ ।  
ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಂ ಕೃತಂ ತೇನ ಸಮಾಸಹಸ್ರಂ ರಹಸ್ಯಮೇತತ್ಪಿತರೋ ವದನ್ತಿ॥೧೪-೧೧೦-೨೯॥  
---ಮಹಾಭಾರತೇ (ಕುಮ್ಭಘೋಣ-ಸಂಸ್ಕರಣಮ್)

f8b7a0f0a4.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in śravaṇaḥ makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°41′10.23″.
f8b7a0f0a4.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°41′10.23″, 0°41′02.86″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 2°00′27.09″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.28, elongation 5°47′33.06″ E). śukraḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°19′16.86″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 5°35′33.69″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

f8ca39f5c2.d:
East India Company British troops under Hugh Gough, aided mostly by superior artillery, smashed rAjA sher-singh's army at Gujrat village near Chenab.

Sher Singh was unable to find sufficient food for his army - his retreat east towards friendly sikh villages was blocked by a swollen Chenab with a few fords defended by irregular Muslim cavalry under British officers. Sher Singh withdrew to Gujrat, where his army hastily prepared a defensive position - alas, the terrain was not as advantageous as in Chillianwala. 96 Field Guns + 67 Siege Guns of the British overwhelmed Sher Singh's 60 guns in a 3 hour battle. The artillery then assisted the British infantry advance. Finally, the cavalry took up a ruthless pursuit, which turned the Sikh retreat into a rout over 12 miles (19 km). 

Aftermath: The remnants of Sher Singh's forces retreated across the Jhelum River and into progressively rougher country with Muslim villagers for eleven days, but Sher Singh was finally forced to agree to British terms for surrender.

f8dfbe41aa.s:
ಸ್ಮೃತಿಮುಕ್ತಾಫಲೇ ವರ್ಣಾಶ್ರಮಧರ್ಮಕಾಣ್ಡೇ  
ಭಾರದ್ವಾಜಃ---  
ವ್ಯತೀಪಾತೇ ವೈಧೃತೌ ಚ ದತ್ತಮಕ್ಷಯಕೃದ್ ಭವೇತ್।  
ದ್ವೌ ತಿಥ್ಯನ್ತಾವೇಕವಾರೇ ಯಸ್ಮಿನ್ ಸ ಸ್ಯಾದ್ ದಿನಕ್ಷಯಃ॥  
ತಸ್ಮಿನ್ ದಾನಂ ಜಪೋ ಹೋಮಃ ಸ್ನಾನಂ ಚೈವ ಫಲಪ್ರದಮ್॥  
ಸಂವರ್ತ್ತಃ---  
ಅಯನೇ ವಿಷುವೇ ಚೈವ ವ್ಯತೀಪಾತೇ ದಿನಕ್ಷಯೇ।  
ಚನ್ದ್ರಸೂರ್ಯಗ್ರಹೇ ಚೈವ ದತ್ತಂ ಭವತಿ ಚಾಕ್ಷಯಮ್॥  
  
ಪುರುಷಾರ್ಥಚಿನ್ತಾಮಣೌ---  
ಹೇಮಾದ್ರೌ ಯಾಜ್ಞವಲ್ಕ್ಯಃ---  
ಶತಮಿನ್ದುಕ್ಷಯೇ ದಾನಂ ಸಹಸ್ರಂ ತು ದಿನಕ್ಷಯೇ।  
ವಿಷುವೇ ದಶಸಾಹಸ್ರಂ ವ್ಯತೀಪಾತೇ ತ್ವನನ್ತಕಮ್॥  
ತತ್ರೈವ ವಾರಾಹಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ದರ್ಶೇ ಶತಗುಣಂ ದಾನಂ ತಚ್ಛತಘ್ನಂ ದಿನಕ್ಷಯೇ।  
  
ಧ್ರುವಚರಿತ-ಪಾರಾಯಣಮ್/ಶ್ರವಣಮ್  
ಪ್ರಯತಃ ಕೀರ್ತಯೇತ್ ಪ್ರಾತಃ ಸಮವಾಯೇ ದ್ವಿಜನ್ಮನಾಮ್।  
ಸಾಯಂ ಚ ಪುಣ್ಯಶ್ಲೋಕಸ್ಯ ಧ್ರುವಸ್ಯ ಚರಿತಂ ಮಹತ್॥೪೮॥  
ಪೌರ್ಣಮಾಸ್ಯಾಂ ಸಿನೀವಾಲ್ಯಾಂ ದ್ವಾದಶ್ಯಾಂ ಶ್ರವಣೇಽಥವಾ।  
ದಿನಕ್ಷಯೇ ವ್ಯತೀಪಾತೇ ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಮೇಽರ್ಕದಿನೇಽಪಿ ವಾ॥೪೯॥  
ಶ್ರಾವಯೇಚ್ಛ್ರದ್ದಧಾನಾನಾಂ ತೀರ್ಥಪಾದಪದಾಶ್ರಯಃ।  
ನೇಚ್ಛಂಸ್ತತ್ರಾತ್ಮನಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಸನ್ತುಷ್ಟ ಇತಿ ಸಿಧ್ಯತಿ॥೫೦॥  
---ಶ್ರೀಮದ್ಭಾಗವತೇ ೪-೧೨  
  
ಕುರ್ಯಾದಪರಪಕ್ಷೀಯಂ ಮಾಸಿ ಪ್ರೌಷ್ಠಪದೇ ದ್ವಿಜಃ।  
ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಂ ಪಿತ್ರೋರ್ಯಥಾವಿತ್ತಂ ತದ್ಬನ್ಧೂನಾಂ ಚ ವಿತ್ತವಾನ್॥೧೯॥  
ಅಯನೇ ವಿಷುವೇ ಕುರ್ಯಾದ್ ವ್ಯತೀಪಾತೇ ದಿನಕ್ಷಯೇ।  
...  
ತ ಏತೇ ಶ್ರೇಯಸಃ ಕಾಲಾ ನೃಣಾಂ ಶ್ರೇಯೋವಿವರ್ಧನಾಃ।  
ಕುರ್ಯಾತ್ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮನೈತೇಷು ಶ್ರೇಯೋಽಮೋಘಂ ತದಾಯುಷಃ॥೨೪॥  
ಏಷು ಸ್‍ನಾನಂ ಜಪೋ ಹೋಮೋ ವ್ರತಂ ದೇವದ್ವಿಜಾರ್ಚನಮ್।  
ಪಿತೃದೇವನೃಭೂತೇಭ್ಯೋ ಯದ್ದತ್ತಂ ತದ್ಧ್ಯನಶ್ವರಮ್॥೨೫॥  
---ಶ್ರೀಮದ್ಭಾಗವತೇ ೭-೧೪

fa6dd14140.s:
ತತೋಽಬ್ರವೀನ್ಮಹಾತೇಜಾ ವ್ಯಾಸೋ ಧರ್ಮಾತ್ಮಜಂ ನೃಪಮ್ ।  
ಯಥಾಕಾಲಂ ಯಥಾಯೋಗಂ ಸಜ್ಜಾಃ ಸ್ಮ ತವ ದೀಕ್ಷಣೇ॥೧೪-೭೨-೧೦॥  
ಅಶ್ವಶ್ಚೋತ್ಸೃಜ್ಯತಾಮದ್ಯ ಪೃಥ್ವ್ಯಾಮಥ ಯಥಾಕ್ರಮಮ್ ।  
ಸುಗುಪ್ತಂ ಚರತಾಂ ಚಾಪಿ ಯಥಾಶಾಸ್ತ್ರಂ ಯಥಾವಿಧಿ॥೧೪-೭೨-೧೨॥  
ಚೈತ್ರ್ಯಾಂ ಹಿ ಪೌರ್ಣಮಾಸ್ಯಾಂ ತು ತವ ದೀಕ್ಷಾ ಭವಿಷ್ಯತಿ ।  
ಸಮ್ಭಾರಾಃ ಸಮ್ಭ್ರಿಯನ್ತಾಂ ಚ ಯಜ್ಞಾರ್ಥಂ ಪುರುಷರ್ಷಭ॥೧೪-೭೨-೪॥  
ವೈಶಮ್ಪಾಯನ ಉವಾಚ ।  
ದೀಕ್ಷಾಕಾಲೇ ತು ಸಮ್ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೇ ತತಸ್ತೇ ಸುಮಹರ್ತ್ವಿಜಃ ।  
ವಿಧಿವದ್ದೀಕ್ಷಯಾಮಾಸುರಶ್ವಮೇಧಾಯ ಪಾರ್ಥಿವಮ್॥೧೪-೭೩-೧॥  
---ಮಹಾಭಾರತೇ (ಕುಮ್ಭಘೋಣ-ಸಂಸ್ಕರಣಮ್)

fab2d80e4b.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between guruḥ and śukraḥ in maghā siṁhaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°29′42.38″.
fab2d80e4b.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°29′42.38″, 0°29′22.49″ apart, disc-to-disc. guruḥ at maghā-4 siṁhaḥ (latitude 0°54′57.49″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.70, elongation 3°59′23.38″ E). śukraḥ at maghā-4 siṁhaḥ (latitude 1°24′39.86″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 4°07′53.04″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śukraḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) guruḥ is taken as jayI over śukraḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

fab84b07f4.b: Partial solar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈7.4 of 12 aṅgulas), Sun at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
fab84b07f4.d: Magnitude: 61% of the solar diameter is covered (parimāṇa ≈7.4 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 03:20►17:52 (from 4 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra punarvasuḥ/puṣyaḥ/āśrēṣā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or anūrādhā (anujanma) or uttaraprōṣṭhapadā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: karkaṭaḥ, siṁhaḥ, dhanuḥ, mēṣaḥ get more ashubha phala, vr̥śchikaḥ, makaraḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam somewhat ashubha, kanyā, tulā, kumbhaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
fab84b07f4.r: - Food-restriction timing and graha-shanti nakshatra/rashi lists follow this pancAnga's "General notes for all grahanas" instructions.

fb6f4aa614.s:

fbac58a158.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between guruḥ and śukraḥ in ārdrā mithunam, center-to-center separation 0°51′43.11″.
fbac58a158.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°51′43.11″, 0°51′20.16″ apart, disc-to-disc. guruḥ at ārdrā-4 mithunam (latitude 0°03′50.76″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.94, elongation 35°43′04.75″ W). śukraḥ at ārdrā-4 mithunam (latitude 0°55′33.86″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.96, elongation 35°43′42.01″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śukraḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) guruḥ is taken as jayI over śukraḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

fbe5ee0537.s:
ಸ್ಕಾನ್ದೇ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕಮಾಸಮಾಹಾತ್ಮ್ಯೇ---  
ಕಾರ್ತಿಕ್ಯಾಂ ಪೂರ್ಣಿಮಾಯಾಂ ತು ಕುರ್ಯಾತ್ತ್ರೈಪುರಮುತ್ಸವಮ್।  
ದೀಪೋ ದೇಯೋಽವಶ್ಯಮೇವ ಸಾಯಂಕಾಲೇ ಶಿವಾಲಯೇ॥  
ತಸ್ಮಿನ್ದಿನೇ ಸರ್ವದೇವೈರ್ದೀಪಾ ದತ್ತಾ ಹರಾಯ ಚ।  
ಸರ್ವಥೈವ ಪ್ರದೇಯಾಶ್ಚ ದೀಪಾಸ್ತು ಹರತುಷ್ಟಯೇ॥  
ವಿಂಶತಿಃ ಸಪ್ತಶತಕಾಃ ಸಹಿತಾ ದೀಪವರ್ತಯಃ।  
ದದದ್ದೀಪಂ ಪೂರ್ಣಿಮಾಯಾಂ ಸರ್ವಪಾಪೈಃ ಪ್ರಮುಚ್ಯತೇ॥  
ಪೌರ್ಣಮಾಸ್ಯಾಂ ತು ಸಂಧ್ಯಾಯಾಂ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಸ್ತ್ರಿಪುರೋತ್ಸವಃ।  
ದದ್ಯಾದನೇನ ಮನ್ತ್ರೇಣ ಪ್ರದೀಪಾಂಶ್ಚ ಸುರಾಲಯೇ॥  
ಕೀಟಾಃ ಪತಂಗಾ ಮಶಕಾಶ್ಚ ವೃಕ್ಷಾ ಜಲೇ ಸ್ಥಲೇ ಯೇ ವಿಚರಂತಿ ಜೀವಾಃ।  
ದೃಷ್ಟ್ವಾ ಪ್ರದೀಪಂ ನ ಚ ಜನ್ಮಭಾಗಿನೋ ಭವಂತು ನಿತ್ಯಂ ಶ್ವಪಚಾ ಹಿ ವಿಪ್ರಾಃ॥  
ಕಾರ್ಯಸ್ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ಪೌರ್ಣಮಾಸ್ಯಾಂ ತ್ರಿಪುರಾಯ ಮಹೋತ್ಸವಃ।  
ಕಾರ್ತಿಕ್ಯಾಂ ಕೃತ್ತಿಕಾಯೋಗೇ ಯಃ ಕುರ್ಯಾತ್ಸ್ವಾಮಿದರ್ಶನಮ್॥  
ಸಪ್ತ ಜನ್ಮ ಭವೇದ್ವಿಪ್ರೋ ಧನಾಢ್ಯೋ ವೇದಪಾರಗಃ।  
+++(The dIpa mantra also circulates with ನಿವಸನ್ತಿ and ಭವನ್ತಿ.)+++

fbef6da151.b: Partial lunar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈2.3 of 12 aṅgulas), Moon at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
fbef6da151.d: The eclipse is already in progress at moonrise (grastodaya). Umbral magnitude: 0.19 (parimāṇa ≈2.3 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 09:38►19:53 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra maghā/pūrvaphalgunī/uttaraphalgunī (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or pūrvāṣāḍhā (anujanma) or apabharaṇī (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: siṁhaḥ, kanyā, makaraḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ get more ashubha phala, dhanuḥ, kumbhaḥ, mēṣaḥ, karkaṭaḥ somewhat ashubha, tulā, vr̥śchikaḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
fbef6da151.r: - Food-restriction timing and graha-shanti nakshatra/rashi lists follow this pancAnga's "General notes for all grahanas" instructions.

fc3a4bc494.s:
ಶ್ರಾವಣಂ ನಿಯತೋ ಮಾಸಮೇಕಭಕ್ತೇನ ಯಃ ಕ್ಷಿಪೇತ್ ।  
ರೂಪದ್ರವಿಣಸಮ್ಪನ್ನಃ ಸುಖೀ ಭವತಿ ನಿತ್ಯಶಃ ।  
ಬಹುಭಾರ್ಯೋ ಬಹುಧನೋ ಬಹುಪುತ್ರಶ್ಚ ಜಾಯತೇ॥೧೩-೧೬೩-೨೬॥  
ಶ್ರಾವಣಂ ಯಃ ಕ್ಷಿಪೇನ್ಮಾಸಮೇಕಭುಕ್ತೇನ ವರ್ತತೇ ।  
ನಮೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣ್ಯದೇವಾಯೇತ್ಯುಕ್ತ್ವಾ ಮಾಮರ್ಚಯೇತ್ಸದಾ ।  
ವಿಪ್ರಮಾಗ್ರಾಸನೇ ಕೃತ್ವಾ ಭೂಮೌ ಭುಞ್ಜನ್ಯಥಾವಿಧಿ॥೧೪-೧೧೩-೪೨॥  
ಪಾಯಸೇನಾರ್ಚಯನ್ವಿಪ್ರಾಞ್ಜಿತಕ್ರೋಧೋ ಜಿತೇನ್ದ್ರಿಯಃ ।  
ಲೋಭಮೋಹವಿನಿರ್ಮುಕ್ತಸ್ತಸ್ಯ ಪುಣ್ಯಫಲಂ ಶೃಣು॥೧೪-೧೧೩-೪೩॥  
ಕಪಿಲಾದಾನಸ್ಯ ಯತ್ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ವಿಧಿದತ್ತಸ್ಯ ಪಾಣ್ಡವ ।

fc675c6385.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between guruḥ and budhaḥ in maghā siṁhaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°37′24.46″.
fc675c6385.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°37′24.46″, 0°37′06.91″ apart, disc-to-disc. guruḥ at maghā-4 siṁhaḥ (latitude 0°54′43.42″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.70, elongation 8°32′36.92″ E). budhaḥ at maghā-4 siṁhaḥ (latitude 1°32′07.88″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.11, elongation 8°37′54.39″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) guruḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

fc9bdb7a29.d: Umbral magnitude: 1.36 (parimāṇa ≈12.0 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 09:20►02:25 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra śatabhiṣak/pūrvaprōṣṭhapadā/uttaraprōṣṭhapadā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or punarvasuḥ (anujanma) or viśākhā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: kumbhaḥ, mīnaḥ, karkaṭaḥ, vr̥śchikaḥ get more ashubha phala, mithunam, siṁhaḥ, tulā, makaraḥ somewhat ashubha, mēṣaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ, kanyā, dhanuḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.

fcab41348d.s:
ಸ್ಮೃತ್ಯನ್ತರೇ---  
ಅಮಾ ಪಾತಶ್ಚ ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತಿಸ್ತಥಾ ವೈಧೃತಿರೇವ ಚ।  
ಅಷ್ಟಕಾಶ್ಚೈವ ಮನ್ವಾದಿರ್ಯುಗಾದಿಶ್ಚ ಮಹಾಲಯಃ॥  
ಚನ್ದ್ರಸೂರ್ಯೋಪರಾಗಶ್ಚ ಗಜಚ್ಛಾಯಾ ತಥೈವ ಚ।  
ದ್ರವ್ಯಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಸಮ್ಪತ್ತಿಃ ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಕಾಲಾಃ ಪ್ರಕೀರ್ತಿತಾಃ॥  
ಮತ್ಸ್ಯಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಕೃತಂ ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಂ ವಿಧಾನೇನ ಮನ್ವಾದಿಷು ಯುಗಾದಿಷು॥  
ಹಾಯನಾನಿ ದ್ವಿಸಾಹಸ್ರಂ ಪಿತೄಣಾಂ ತೃಪ್ತಿದಂ ಭವೇತ್।  
ಆಸು ಸ್ನಾನಂ ಜಪೋ ಹೋಮಃ ಪುಣ್ಯಾನನ್ತ್ಯಾಯ ಕಲ್ಪತೇ॥  
ಮಹಾಭಾರತೇಽಪಿ---   
ಯಾ ಮನ್ವಾದ್ಯಾ ಯುಗಾದ್ಯಾಶ್ಚ ತಿಥಯಸ್ತಾಸು ಮಾನವಃ।  
ಸ್ನಾತ್ವಾ ಭುಕ್ತ್ವಾ ಚ ದತ್ತ್ವಾ ಚ ತದನನ್ತಫಲಂ ಲಭೇತ್॥  
ಕಾಲಾದರ್ಶೇಽಪಿ---  
ಮನ್ವಾದ್ಯಾಸು ಯುಗಾದ್ಯಾಸು ಪ್ರದತ್ತಃ ಸಲಿಲಾಞ್ಜಲಿಃ।  
ಸಹಸ್ರವಾರ್ಷಿಕೀ ತೃಪ್ತಿಂ ಪಿತೄಣಾಮಾವಹೇತ್ ಪರಾಮ್॥  
ದ್ವಿಸಹಸ್ರಾಬ್ದಿಕೀ ತೃಪ್ತಿಂ ಕೃತಂ ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಂ ಯಥಾವಿಧಿ।  
ಸ್ನಾನಂ ದಾನಂ ಜಪೋ ಹೋಮಃ ಪುಣ್ಯಾನನ್ತ್ಯಾಯ ಕಲ್ಪತೇ॥  
ಪುರುಷಾರ್ಥಚಿನ್ತಾಮಣೌ ಮನುಃ---  
ಸಹಸ್ರಗುಣಿತಂ ದಾನಂ ಭವೇದ್ದತ್ತಂ ಯುಗಾದಿಷು।  
ಕರ್ಮ ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಾದಿಕಂ ಚೈವ ತಥಾ ಮನ್ವನ್ತರಾದಿಷು॥

fd3cf880bc.d:
A massacre and rape of the Hindu population of Bakhrabad village, in the district of the Comilla, on 24 May 1971 by the Pakistani army with the help of Al Badr and Al Shams.

The attackers went from house to house, indiscriminately killing men, women, and children. They also set fire to homes and looted the village. The attack lasted for several hours, and by the time it was over, hundreds of people were dead.

Aftermath
The Bakhrabad massacre was widely reported in the international media, which put pressure on the Pakistani government to end the violence. However, the Pakistani military continued its campaign of terror in Bangladesh, which led to the deaths of millions of people.

ಪೂರ್ಣೇ ಚತುರ್ದಶೇ ವರ್ಷೇ ಪಞ್ಚಮ್ಯಾಂ ಲಕ್ಷ್ಮಣಾಗ್ರಜಃ।

fd7797c6e8.d: While this is traditionally celebrated in Dhanurmasa, given the precession of equinoxes, it would be ideal to celebrate it in the corresponding tropical solar month, given that is the start of the uṣahkāla for the Devatas. A very early morning puja is performed, typically with mudgānnam as naivedyam. Begets fruit equivalent to performing puja for a thousand years! The two ayana-s of the Sun are night and day for the Devas. 30 of these days become a month. The uṣahkāla of their day starts in chāpamāsa i.e. dhanurmāsa (although the shloka refers to the sidereal month, it appears logical to use the tropical month, owing to its association with uttarāyaṇam). Therefore, one must strive to perform uṣahkāla-pujā in this month, before sunrise --- a ṣōḍaśōpachāra-pūjā. Following this, one must perform Sandhyavandam and upasthanam! The Shivapurana also extols the uniqueness of the early morning puja in this month, suggesting that one must perform rudrābhiṣeka.
fd7797c6e8.s:
ಭಾಸ್ಕರೀಯೇ---  
ಅಯನಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ರಾತ್ರಿರುತ್ತರಂ ತು ದಿವಾ ಭವೇತ್।  
ದೈವತಂ ತದಹೋರಾತ್ರಂ ತತ್ ತ್ರಿಂಶನ್ಮಾಸ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ॥  
ತದ್ದಿನಸ್ಯ ಉಷಃಕಾಲಂ ಚಾಪಮಾಸಂ ವಿದುರ್ಬುಧಾಃ।  
ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಯತ್ನೇನ ಚಾಪಮಾಸೇ ದಿನೇ ದಿನೇ॥  
ಉಷಃಕಾಲೇ ತು ಸಮ್ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೇ ಬೋಧಯಿತ್ವಾ ಜನಾರ್ದನಮ್।  
ಸಮಭ್ಯರ್ಚ್ಯ ಭಜೇದ್ವಿಷ್ಣುಂ ಜನಾನಾಂ ದೋಷಶಾನ್ತಯೇ॥  
ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಾಣ್ಡಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಉಷಃಕಾಲೇ ತು ಸಮ್ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೇ ಅರ್ಚಯಿತ್ವಾ ಜನಾರ್ದನಮ್।  
ಉಪಚಾರೈಃ ಷೋಡಶಭಿರ್ಮುದ್ಗಾನ್ನಂ ಚ ನಿವೇದಯೇತ್॥  
ಆದಿತ್ಯ ಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಉಷಃಕಾಲೇ ತು ಸಮ್ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೇ ಪ್ರತ್ಯೂಷೇ ಸ್ನಾನಮಾಚರೇತ್।  
ಅರ್ಚಯೇಚ್ಚ ಜಗನ್ನಾಥಂ ಯಾವತ್ಸೂರ್ಯೋದಯಾತ್ಪುರಾ॥  
ತತಃ ಪ್ರಭಾತಸಮಯೇ ಅರ್ಘ್ಯಂ ಪ್ರಕ್ಷಿಪ್ಯ ವೈ ದ್ವಿಜಃ।  
ಗಾಯತ್ರೀಂ ಚ ತತೋ ಜಪ್ತ್ವಾ ಉಪತಿಷ್ಠೇತ ಭಾಸ್ಕರಮ್॥  
ಶಿವಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಚಾಪರಾಶೌ ಸ್ಥಿತೇ ಸೂರ್ಯೇ ಉಷಃಕಾಲೇ ದಿನೇ ದಿನೇ।  
ಅಭಿಷೇಕಂ ತತಃ ಕುರ್ಯಾದ್ರೌದ್ರಮನ್ತ್ರೇಣ ರುದ್ರವಿತ್॥  
ಅರ್ಕಪುಷ್ಪೈಶ್ಚ ಬಿಲ್ವೈಶ್ಚ ಪೂಜಯೇಚ್ಚ ಮಹೇಶ್ವರಮ್।  
ನೈವೇದ್ಯಂ ಚ ತತಃ ಕುರ್ಯಾತ್ ಲೋಕಸಂಹಾರ ಶಾನ್ತಯೇ॥  
ಅನ್ಯತ್ರ---  
ಕೋದಣ್ಡಸ್ಥೇ ಸವಿತರಿ ಪ್ರತ್ಯೂಷೇ ಪೂಜಯೇದ್ಧರೇಃ।  
ಸಹಸ್ರಾಬ್ದಾರ್ಚನಫಲಂ ದಿನೇನೈಕೇನ ಲಭ್ಯತೇ॥

As stated in the Mahābhārata:
- Narrative: Yudhiṣṭhira's dīkṣā for the Rājasūya on the amāvāsyā of Jyeṣṭhāmūla (MBh 2.36.45, 2.36.46, 2.36.47) +++(passage marked additional in the Kumbhakonam text)+++
fd8da2706e.s:
ತತಸ್ತೇ ತು ಯಥಾಕಾಲಂ ಕುನ್ತೀಪುತ್ರಂ ಯುಧಿಷ್ಠಿರಮ್ ।  
ದೀಕ್ಷಯಾಞ್ಚಕ್ರಿರೇ ವಿಪ್ರಾ ರಾಜಸೂಯಾಯ ಭಾರತ॥೨-೩೬-೪೫॥  
`ಜ್ಯೇಷ್ಠಾಮೂಲೇ ಅಮಾವಾಸ್ಯಾಂ ಮೃಗಾಜಿನಸಮಾವೃತಃ ।  
ರೌರವಾಜಿನಸಂವೀತೋ ನವನೀತಾಕ್ತದೇಹವಾನ್'॥೨-೩೬-೪೬॥  
ದೀಕ್ಷಿತಃ ಸ ತು ಧರ್ಮಾತ್ಮಾ ಧರ್ಮರಾಜೋ ಯುಧಿಷ್ಠಿರಃ ।  
ಜಗಾಮ ಯಜ್ಞಾಯತನಂ ವೃತೋ ವಿಪ್ರೈಃ ಸಹಸ್ರಶಃ॥೨-೩೬-೪೭॥

---ನಿರ್ಣಯಸಿನ್ಧುಃ  
ಕನ್ಯಾಪ್ರವೇಶೇ ವಸ್ತ್ರಾಣಾಂ ಸುರಭೀಣಾಂ ತಥೈವ ಚ॥   
---ಸ್ಮೃತಿಕೌಸ್ತುಭೇ  
ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತಿಸ್ನಾನಾಕರಣೇ ಪ್ರತ್ಯವಾಯಮಾಹ ಶಾತಾತಪಃ—  
ಸೂರ್ಯಸಙ್ಕ್ರಮಣೇ ಪುಣ್ಯೇ ನ ಸ್ನಾಯಾದ್ಯದಿ ಮಾನವಃ।  
ಸಪ್ತಜನ್ಮಸು ರೋಗೀ ಸ್ಯಾದ್ ದುಃಖಭಾಗೀ ಚ ಜಾಯತೇ॥  
ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತ್ಯಾಂ ಯಾನಿ ದತ್ತಾನಿ ಹವ್ಯಕವ್ಯಾನಿ ಮಾನವೈಃ।  
ತಾನಿ ತಸ್ಯ ದದಾತ್ಯರ್ಕಃ ಸಪ್ತಜನ್ಮಸು ನಿಶ್ಚಿತಮ್॥  
---ವೈದ್ಯನಾಥ-ದೀಕ್ಷಿತೀಯೇ ಸ್ಮೃತಿಮುಕ್ತಾಫಲೇ ಆಹ್ನಿಕ-ಕಾಣ್ಡಃ (ಪೂರ್ವಭಾಗಃ)  
ಷಡಶೀತ್ಯಾಂ ತು ಯದ್ದತ್ತಂ ಯದ್ದತ್ತಂ ವಿಷುವದ್ವಯೇ।  
ದೃಶ್ಯತೇ ಸಾಗರಸ್ಯಾನ್ತಸ್ತಸ್ಯಾನ್ತೋ ನೈವ ದೃಶ್ಯತೇ॥  
---ಸ್ಮೃತಿಕೌಸ್ತುಭೇ  
ಷಡಶೀತ್ಯಾಮತೀತಾಯಾಂ ಷಷ್ಟಿರುಕ್ತಾಸ್ತು ನಾಡಿಕಾಃ॥  
ಯಾ ಯಾಃ ಸನ್ನಿಹಿತಾ ನಾಡ್ಯಸ್ತಾಸ್ತಾಃ ಪುಣ್ಯತಮಾಃ ಸ್ಮೃತಾಃ॥  
---ವೈದ್ಯನಾಥ-ದೀಕ್ಷಿತೀಯೇ ಸ್ಮೃತಿಮುಕ್ತಾಫಲೇ ಆಹ್ನಿಕ-ಕಾಣ್ಡಃ (ಪೂರ್ವಭಾಗಃ)

fda2315980.d: Preceptor Mahādevendra adorned the Pīṭha for thirty-nine years and attained Siddhi on the new moon day in the month of Phālguṇa of the year Virodhi. This preceptor’s name before initiation was Mahāliṅgam. His parents were well-known as Subbulakṣmī and Śeṣādri. His place of siddhi was a village called Ilayāttaṅguḍi. Śalivahana era 1813. The adhishthanam is located at https://maps.app.goo.gl/aKwrZHNJaMhUSxZc9.
fda2315980.s:
ಮಧ್ಯಾರ್ಜುನಮಹಾಲಿಙ್ಗನಾಮಾ ಹಾರೀತಗೋತ್ರಜಃ।  
ಶೇಷಾದ್ರಿಶಾಸ್ತ್ರಿಣಃ ಸುಬ್ಬುಲಕ್ಷ್ಮ್ಯಾಂ ಪತ್ನ್ಯಾಂ ವ್ಯಜಾಯತ॥೧೬॥  
ಉಪಷಷ್ಟೇ ಸ್ವವಯಸಿ ವಿಶ್ರಮಗ್ರಾಮಮ್ ಆಗತಃ।  
ಶಿವಾಲಯಾನ್ತಿಕೇ ತತ್ರ ಶೈವಂ ಭಾವಮ್ ಉಪಾಗಮತ್॥೧೭॥  
ಪೀಠೇ ಮಹಾದೇವೇನ್ದ್ರಾಖ್ಯಸ್ತ್ರಿಂಶನ್ನವ ಸಮಾಃ ಸ್ಥಿತಃ।  
ವಿರೋಧಿಫಾಲ್ಗುನಾಮಾಯಾಂ ಗುರುಃ ಕೈವಲ್ಯಮ್ ಆಸ್ಥಿತಃ॥೧೮॥  
—ಪುಣ್ಯಶ್ಲೋಕಮಞ್ಜರೀ ಪರಿಶಿಷ್ಟಮ್

fde83a2196.b: Total lunar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈12.0 of 12 aṅgulas), Moon at the Rahu node (mukha/ascending).
fde83a2196.d: Umbral magnitude: 1.36 (parimāṇa ≈12.0 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 09:04►02:25 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra śatabhiṣak/pūrvaprōṣṭhapadā/uttaraprōṣṭhapadā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or punarvasuḥ (anujanma) or viśākhā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: kumbhaḥ, mīnaḥ, karkaṭaḥ, vr̥śchikaḥ get more ashubha phala, mithunam, siṁhaḥ, tulā, makaraḥ somewhat ashubha, mēṣaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ, kanyā, dhanuḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. fe086486f1.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between aṅgārakaḥ and budhaḥ in uttarāṣāḍhā makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°41′04.24″.
fe086486f1.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°41′04.24″, 0°40′59.38″ apart, disc-to-disc. aṅgārakaḥ at uttarāṣāḍhā-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°06′39.26″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +1.17, elongation 16°01′16.47″ E). budhaḥ at uttarāṣāḍhā-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°47′43.50″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -0.85, elongation 16°04′53.45″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) budhaḥ is taken as jayI over aṅgārakaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

fe7a57a69b.s:
ಸ್ಮೃತ್ಯನ್ತರೇ---  
ಅಮಾ ಪಾತಶ್ಚ ಸಙ್ಕ್ರಾನ್ತಿಸ್ತಥಾ ವೈಧೃತಿರೇವ ಚ।  
ಅಷ್ಟಕಾಶ್ಚೈವ ಮನ್ವಾದಿರ್ಯುಗಾದಿಶ್ಚ ಮಹಾಲಯಃ॥  
ಚನ್ದ್ರಸೂರ್ಯೋಪರಾಗಶ್ಚ ಗಜಚ್ಛಾಯಾ ತಥೈವ ಚ।  
ದ್ರವ್ಯಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಸಮ್ಪತ್ತಿಃ ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಕಾಲಾಃ ಪ್ರಕೀರ್ತಿತಾಃ॥  
ಮನ್ವನ್ತರಾದಯೋ ಮತ್ಸ್ಯಪುರಾಣೇ ದರ್ಶಿತಾಃ---  
ಆಶ್ವಯುಕ್ಛುಕ್ಲನವಮೀ ಕಾರ್ತಿಕೀ ದ್ವಾದಶೀ ಸಿತಾ।  
ತೃತೀಯಾ ಚೈತ್ರಮಾಸಸ್ಯ ಸಿತಾ ಭಾದ್ರಪದಸ್ಯ ಚ॥  
ಫಾಲ್ಗುನಸ್ಯಾಪ್ಯಮಾವಾಸ್ಯಾ ಪುಷ್ಯಸ್ಯೈಕಾದಶೀ ಸಿತಾ।  
ಆಷಾಢಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ದಶಮೀ ಮಾಘಮಾಸಸ್ಯ ಸಪ್ತಮೀ॥  
ಶ್ರಾವಣಸ್ಯಾಷ್ಟಮೀ ಕೃಷ್ಣಾ ತಥಾಽಽಷಾಢೀ ಚ ಪೂರ್ಣಿಮಾ।  
ಕಾರ್ತಿಕೀ ಫಾಲ್ಗುನೀ ಚೈತ್ರೀ ಜ್ಯೈಷ್ಠೀ ಪಞ್ಚದಶೀ ಸಿತಾ॥  
ಮನ್ವನ್ತರಾದಯಶ್ಚೈತೇ ದತ್ತಸ್ಯಾಕ್ಷಯಕಾರಕಾಃ।  
ಕೃತಂ ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಂ ವಿಧಾನೇನ ಮನ್ವಾದಿಷು ಯುಗಾದಿಷು॥  
ಹಾಯನಾನಿ ದ್ವಿಸಾಹಸ್ರಂ ಪಿತೄಣಾಂ ತೃಪ್ತಿದಂ ಭವೇತ್।  
ಆಸು ಸ್ನಾನಂ ಜಪೋ ಹೋಮಃ ಪುಣ್ಯಾನನ್ತ್ಯಾಯ ಕಲ್ಪತೇ॥  
ಮಹಾಭಾರತೇಽಪಿ---   
ಯಾ ಮನ್ವಾದ್ಯಾ ಯುಗಾದ್ಯಾಶ್ಚ ತಿಥಯಸ್ತಾಸು ಮಾನವಃ।  
ಸ್ನಾತ್ವಾ ಭುಕ್ತ್ವಾ ಚ ದತ್ತ್ವಾ ಚ ತದನನ್ತಫಲಂ ಲಭೇತ್॥  
ಕಾಲಾದರ್ಶೇಽಪಿ---  
ಮನ್ವಾದ್ಯಾಸು ಯುಗಾದ್ಯಾಸು ಪ್ರದತ್ತಃ ಸಲಿಲಾಞ್ಜಲಿಃ।  
ಸಹಸ್ರವಾರ್ಷಿಕೀ ತೃಪ್ತಿಂ ಪಿತೄಣಾಮಾವಹೇತ್ ಪರಾಮ್॥  
ದ್ವಿಸಹಸ್ರಾಬ್ದಿಕೀ ತೃಪ್ತಿಂ ಕೃತಂ ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಂ ಯಥಾವಿಧಿ।  
ಸ್ನಾನಂ ದಾನಂ ಜಪೋ ಹೋಮಃ ಪುಣ್ಯಾನನ್ತ್ಯಾಯ ಕಲ್ಪತೇ॥  
ಪುರುಷಾರ್ಥಚಿನ್ತಾಮಣೌ ಮನುಃ---  
ಸಹಸ್ರಗುಣಿತಂ ದಾನಂ ಭವೇದ್ದತ್ತಂ ಯುಗಾದಿಷು।  
ಕರ್ಮ ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಾದಿಕಂ ಚೈವ ತಥಾ ಮನ್ವನ್ತರಾದಿಷು॥

ಚತುರ್ದಶ್ಯಾಂ ನಿಶಾಯಾಂ ತು ನಿವೃತ್ತೋ ಮಾಗಧಃ ಕ್ಲಮಾತ್॥೨-೨೪-೩೪॥  
ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ತೇಽದ್ಯೈವ ಕೌನ್ತೇಯ ಪೀಡನೀಯೋ ಜನಾಧಿಪಃ ।  
ಸಮಮೇತೇನ ಯುಧ್ಯಸ್ವ ಬಾಹುಭ್ಯಾಂ ಭರತರ್ಷಭ॥೨-೨೪-೩೭॥  
ಪ್ರಭಞ್ಜನಬಲಾವಿಷ್ಟೋ ಜರಾಸನ್ಧಮರಿನ್ದಮಃ ।  
ಉತ್ಕ್ಷಿಪ್ಯ ಭ್ರಾಮಯಾಮಾಸ ಬಲವನ್ತಂ ಮಹಾಬಲಃ॥೨-೨೫-೯॥  
ಭ್ರಾಮಯಿತ್ವಾ ಶತಗುಣಂ ಜಾನುಭ್ಯಾಂ ಭರತರ್ಷಭ ।  
ಬಭಞ್ಜ ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ ಸಙ್ಕ್ಷಿಪ್ಯ ನಿಷ್ಪಿಷ್ಯ ವಿನನಾದ ಚ॥೨-೨೫-೧೦॥

ff1e33a9d5.b: Observed on Śukla-Daśamī tithi of Āśvayujaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).

ff28c9dd44.d:
On this day, raNajIt singh and his generals (including hari singh) defeated afghAn jihAdi-s and captured peshAvar valley. Azem Khan, after initial attacks, retreated and stayed on the other side of kAbul river - abandoning his ghAzi-s.

Context
Angered by his defeats, Azem Khan recaptured Peshawar in 1822, he made a call for jihad against the Sikhs; destroyed the Attock bridge and trapped Sikh garrisons west of the sindhu.  Ranjit Singh had already reinforced his forces in Nowshera. Ranjit Singh personally came down and crossed the sindhu under fierce attacks.

Aftermath
The tribesman of Khattaks and Yousafzais suffered enormous casualties due to the Sikh artillery. Swiftly securing Nowshera, Ranjit Singh's forces captured Peshawar and reached Jamrud itself.

ff5160a08a.b: Observed on Śukla-Prathamā tithi of Mārgaśīrṣaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
ff5160a08a.d: Mārgaśīrṣa-māsaḥ begins today --- इn the Mahābhārata, it is said that one who observes the month of Mārgaśīrṣa with ekabhakta discipline (eating only once a day), and offers food to brāhmaṇas with devotion, is freed from all sins. Such a person becomes wealthy, prosperous in agriculture, and blessed with abundant grains. In the Vāmana Purāṇa, it is stated that to please Keśava (Viṣṇu) during the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, one should make offerings such as donkeys, camels, horses, elephants, cows, carts, and goats/sheep.
ff5160a08a.s:

ಮಾರ್ಗಶೀರ್ಷಂ ತು ಯೋ ಮಾಸಮೇಕಭಕ್ತೇನ ಸಙ್ಕ್ಷಿಪೇತ್।  
ಭೋಜಯೇತ್ತು ದ್ವಿಜಾನ್ಭಕ್ತ್ಯಾ ಸರ್ವಪಾಪೈಃ ಪ್ರಮುಚ್ಯತೇ॥  
ಕೃಷಿಭಾಗೀ (ಕೃಷೀ ಭೋಗೀ) ಬಹುಧನೋ ಬಹುಧಾನ್ಯಶ್ಚ ಜಾಯತೇ॥  
ವಾಮನಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಖರೋಷ್ಟ್ರಾಶ್ವಗಜಾ ಗಾವಃ ಶಕಟಾದಿ ಅಜಾವಿಕಮ್।  
ದಾತವ್ಯಂ ಕೇಶವಪ್ರೀತ್ಯೈ ಮಾಸಿ ಮಾರ್ಗಶಿರೇ ನರೈಃ॥ ಇತಿ।

A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

fff65cd294.d: Magnitude: 9% of the solar diameter is covered (parimāṇa ≈1.0 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 17:03►10:44 (from 4 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra uttarāṣāḍhā/śravaṇaḥ/śraviṣṭhā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or rōhiṇī (anujanma) or hastaḥ (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: makaraḥ, kumbhaḥ, mithunam, tulā get more ashubha phala, vr̥ṣabhaḥ, karkaṭaḥ, kanyā, dhanuḥ somewhat ashubha, mīnaḥ, mēṣaḥ, siṁhaḥ, vr̥śchikaḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
